boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UC Berkeley destinations for reading, creating, recreation, campus services, and student-organization work.

cards.title: Doe Library
cards.subtitle: Central campus library and research space
cards.notes: Start at the Reference Center for a large-table work session, then use its research computers, printing, scanning, or librarian help as needed.
cards.short_summary: A central library building with historic reading rooms, research support, and student workspaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Doe Library’s Reference Center includes the North Reading Room, Reference Hall, and Heyns Reading Room, plus study tables, research computers, printing, and scanning.
cards.access_notes: Open to Berkeley students, faculty, staff, and the public; some rooms and services have separate eligibility rules.

cards.title: Heyns Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Doe Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing work to the second-floor tables, and check the current library hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: One of Doe’s large-table reading rooms, shared with current periodicals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Heyns Reading Room is on Floor 2 of Doe Library and is one of the two rooms providing more than 400 seats at large study tables.
cards.access_notes: Located in Doe Library; the library’s current hours and access policies apply.

cards.title: North Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Doe Library, Floor 2
cards.notes: Use the large study tables for focused reading or laptop work; bring an outlet adapter if you need power at these tables.
cards.short_summary: A historic Doe Library reading room with study tables and limited comfortable seating.
cards.evidence_claim: The North Reading Room on Doe Library’s Floor 2 provides study seating at large tables; its tables may require outlet adapters.
cards.access_notes: Located in Doe Library; the library’s current hours and access policies apply.

cards.title: Morrison Library
cards.subtitle: 101 Doe Library
cards.notes: Leave the laptop behind and settle in with a book, magazine, audiobook, or reading tablet when you want a keyboard-free break.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, laptop-free reading room with popular books, magazines, and music collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Morrison Library offers comfortable reading seating and is laptop-free for patrons studying or reading without keyboard noise.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; laptops are not permitted, though tablets used for reading are allowed.

cards.title: Main (Gardner) Stacks
cards.subtitle: Connected to Doe Library
cards.notes: Enter through Doe to browse the stacks or work near the collections; use the library’s current-hours page before an evening visit.
cards.short_summary: The large underground collections building linked directly to Doe Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main (Gardner) Stacks are connected to Doe Library and house the collections of Doe and Moffitt libraries.
cards.access_notes: Enter via Doe Library; the Library notes that Cal ID is required for Main Stacks access after 7 p.m.

cards.entity_name: Martin Luther King Jr. Student Union
cards.title: Martin Luther King Jr. Student Union
cards.subtitle: 2495 Bancroft Way
cards.notes: Use the information desk to orient yourself, then visit the building’s student services, creative programs, or scheduled campus activities.
cards.short_summary: A campus-life building that houses student-facing programs, services, and event space.
cards.evidence_claim: The MLK Jr. Student Union hosts student-related activities, programs, and services and contains the Berkeley Art Studio and Creative Lab.
cards.source_title: Contact Us | Student Union at UC Berkeley
cards.access_notes: The lobby is open to guests during operating hours; access beyond it can require UC Berkeley affiliation and Cal 1 identification.

cards.title: Eshleman Hall
cards.subtitle: 2465 Bancroft Way
cards.notes: Check the Student Union building map or information desk before meeting a student organization or finding a campus service in the building.
cards.short_summary: A Student Union building used for student government, services, organization space, and campus functions.
cards.evidence_claim: Eshleman Hall was constructed to house student government and services, and the ASUC may allocate its space for student-related activities, programs, and services.
cards.source_title: Statement of Understanding: The ASUC | Division of Student Affairs
cards.access_notes: Building access and available spaces are subject to Student Union policies and current operating hours.

cards.title: Creative Lab
cards.subtitle: MLK Jr. Student Union, Suite 155
cards.notes: Bring a print or design project and ask about available print, design, or class services before placing a paid order or enrolling.
cards.short_summary: A Student Union creative-services space for design, printing, and design classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Creative Lab is in Suite 155 on the first floor of the MLK Jr. Student Union and offers print and design services and design classes.
cards.source_title: Creative Programs | Student Union at UC Berkeley
cards.access_notes: The Creative Lab lists Suite 155 in MLK Jr. Student Union; services and classes may have separate terms or charges.

cards.title: Berkeley Art Studio
cards.subtitle: MLK Jr. Student Union, first floor
cards.notes: Review the current course listings, then choose a medium such as ceramics, photography, drawing, painting, design, or printmaking.
cards.short_summary: A campus art-program space offering classes across several studio media.
cards.evidence_claim: The Berkeley Art Studio is on MLK Jr.’s first floor and offers classes in ceramics, photography, drawing, painting, design, and printmaking.
cards.source_title: Creative Programs | Student Union at UC Berkeley
cards.access_notes: Registration is open to UC Berkeley students, faculty, staff, and the community; course enrollment may require payment.

cards.title: Student Environmental Resource Center
cards.subtitle: MLK Student Union, bNorth, Suite 82C3
cards.notes: Stop by to connect with sustainability resources or organizations, and check its programs before planning a meeting or project collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A majority student-led campus department supporting environmental and sustainability work.
cards.evidence_claim: SERC is a majority student-led campus department that supports students and student organizations through climate, sustainability, and environmental programs and initiatives.
cards.access_notes: Located at 2495 Bancroft Way, Suite 82C3; verify current availability or programming directly with SERC.
